findings.body: GNU sed does not support the BSD `-i ''` form, so the replacement fails and the existing webhook URL remains unchanged despite the script subsequently announcing success.
findings.failure_mode: Existing webhook configuration cannot be updated on Linux.
findings.impact: GNU sed does not support the BSD `-i ''` form, so the replacement fails and the existing webhook URL remains unchanged despite the script subsequently announcing success.
findings.root_cause: The script hard-codes BSD sed's separate empty backup suffix syntax.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a portable temporary-file replacement, or select the BSD/GNU in-place syntax based on the platform and check the command result.
findings.title: Use a sed invocation that works on GNU/Linux
findings.trigger: Running the script on GNU/Linux when GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is already present in the env file.
findings.verifier_reason: Line R68 shows `sed -i '' -E` which is BSD sed syntax. GNU sed requires `sed -i -E` (no space after -i for no backup). This will fail on Linux systems.

pr.body:
## Summary This pull request introduces a new feature to manage calendar cache data, including the ability to view cache status and delete cached data. It also includes several supporting updates to repositories, APIs, and UI components. Below is a summary of the most important changes grouped by theme. ### New Feature: Calendar Cache Management * Added a `deleteCache` mutation to the TRPC `calendarsRouter`, enabling users to delete cached calendar data by credential ID. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsxR27-R33](diffhunk://#diff-9e053175cc6dfb5717313e0587a730fff132f9d3c1200204f0ce8dac53a19280R27-R33)`) * Introduced the `deleteCacheHandler` to handle cache deletion logic, including validation of user access to the specified credential. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.tsR1-R33](diffhunk://#diff-572888b8e0555167a5787847f29d5a46623eff170491acc0654e916f5b4afd18R1-R33)`) * Updated the `connectedCalendarsHandler` to enrich calendar data with cache status (`cacheUpdatedAt`) by querying the `CalendarCacheRepository`. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.tsR27-R39](diffhunk://#diff-3f6a556ad60f26d0162770fcd81b5bddeb6ab0437552ac792045c3cd2608d710R27-R39)`) ### UI Enhancements * Created a new `CredentialActionsDropdown` component to display cache status and provide options to delete cached data or disconnect integrations. (`[packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsxR1-R134](diffhunk://#diff-c78273434b95ab8276bb5eb24d9bc088b10af029388bdcd08cbe478f44269b31R1-R134)`) * Replaced the `DisconnectIntegration` component with `CredentialActionsDropdown` in the `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` UI, integrating the new cache management functionality. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L5-R5)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L70-L81)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L125-L135)`) ### Repository and Database Updates * Added a `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method to the `CalendarCacheRepository` and its mock implementation to fetch cache statuses for multiple credentials. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b36c72c0db751ba0cafe234dfa150817672869825333c22b074c4977a6135b8dR30-R32)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ceffbae9ef3da413495feac73a341672e77ffaf493cf67ada0b637ead80ded38R26-R30)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4cf8d3089fad7b6c8fe4172d8d42147f136b65baf30b726e57b9b10d179d4a99R172-R188)`) * Introduced a new `updateManyByCredentialId` method in the `SelectedCalendarRepository` to update multiple calendars by credential ID. (`[packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.tsR400-R406](diffhunk://#diff-ccb4eecfa701e5b0c7d6ba87dcc550cdf3700a63ee252849045611599ecb9273R400-R406)`) * Added an `updatedAt` column to the `CalendarCache` table in the database schema and Prisma model to track the last update timestamp. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f597bd98bbcfdcf4861ee7bf0c238e7dfe54b456ceb69b852aaf3979c4102cfR1-R8)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-56fa4d384ba6fb94b130e9eb42c5cad00734b025ebd6c197f76873469725ae87R1718)`) ### Localization and Strings * Added new localization strings for cache management actions, such as "Cache Status," "Delete cached data," and "Cache deleted successfully." (`[apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.jsonR3376-R3382](diffhunk://#diff-57de4b8e5231f1d699891d98b0381d56e9e24537b0ca5420d1fba4f0597370bcR3376-R3382)`) ### Miscellaneous * Updated `package.json` to replace `ts-node` with `npx tsx` for running the `dev:cron` script. (`[apps/web/package.jsonL11-R11](diffhunk://#diff-14b60f636e1a2b0061da57aaf231cb1ed15a5dc0c592425ed82e58fec95d42d8L11-R11)`) ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human **🔴 High Priority (5 items)** - [x] **Verify deleteCache tRPC mutation exists** - The component references `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache.useMutation()` but this mutation implementation is not visible in the PR changes. Check if this endpoint exists or needs to be created. - [x] **End-to-end testing with Google Calendar** - Install a Google Calendar integration and verify the credential-level dropdown appears, shows cache status, and deletion flow works correctly with confirmation dialog. - [x] **Test cache status display logic** - Verify that `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamps are correctly formatted and displayed only for Google Calendar credentials with actual cache data. - [x] **Confirm repository pattern correctness** - Test that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` returns accurate data and the credential-to-cache mapping works properly in the UI. - [x] **Verify dropdown conditional rendering** - Ensure the dropdown only appears for Google Calendar credentials and handles edge cases (no cache, disabled integrations, etc.). **Recommended Test Plan:** 1. Connect a Google Calendar integration to trigger cache creation 2. Navigate to `/apps/installed/calendar` 3. Verify dropdown appears on Google Calendar credential with cache status and timestamp 4. Test "Delete cached data" action shows confirmation dialog 5. Confirm cache deletion works and UI updates appropriately 6. Test "Remove App" functionality still works correctly --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD UI["CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx
(New Component)"]:::major-edit Handler["connectedCalendars.handler.ts
(Updated tRPC Handler)"]:::major-edit RepoInterface["calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts
(Updated Interface)"]:::minor-edit RepoImpl["calendar-cache.repository.ts
(Updated Implementation)"]:::minor-edit RepoMock["calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts
(Updated Mock)"]:::minor-edit Translations["common.json
(Added Translation Keys)"]:::minor-edit UI -->|"Uses repository via tRPC"| Handler Handler -->|"Calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds"| RepoImpl RepoImpl -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface RepoMock -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface UI -->|"Uses translation keys"| Translations subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes - **Session Details**: Requested by @zomars, implemented in Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/24545e0980df465995521419432a2a52 - **SelectedCalendar.updatedAt Usage**: Currently only updated in backend via Google webhook handler but not displayed in frontend. Frontend uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache. Consider if SelectedCalendar.updatedAt update should be removed. - **Import Path Resolution**: Had to fix UI component import paths during development - watch for potential module resolution issues in different environments. - **Testing Limitation**: Local testing was limited due to no installed calendar integrations - end-to-end verification with real Google Calendar data is essential.

raw_findings.body: Every pre-existing cache entry is reported as last updated at migration time rather than when its availability data was actually fetched, so the new cache-status UI presents incorrect freshness information until each entry is rewritten.
raw_findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();
raw_findings.failure_mode: Historical cache freshness is overwritten with the deployment timestamp and then exposed as a real last-update time.
raw_findings.impact: Every pre-existing cache entry is reported as last updated at migration time rather than when its availability data was actually fetched, so the new cache-status UI presents incorrect freshness information until each entry is rewritten.
raw_findings.root_cause: The non-null column is added with a NOW() default, which PostgreSQL applies to existing rows during the migration.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Backfill legacy rows from a meaningful existing timestamp (for example, derive it from expiresAt and the cache lifetime where valid), or mark their status unknown; reserve NOW() for newly created rows.
raw_findings.title: Backfill legacy cache timestamps instead of using the migration time
raw_findings.trigger: Deploying this migration to a database that already contains CalendarCache rows, then viewing cache status for one of those credentials.

raw_findings.root_cause: The generated warning was retained after the migration SQL was changed to add a default.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Delete or update the generated warning so it accurately states that the column is added with a default.

raw_findings.body: The script writes to the parent directory's .env instead of the repository .env, so the local application does not receive the configured GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A successful-looking run modifies an unrelated environment file.
raw_findings.impact: The script writes to the parent directory's .env instead of the repository .env, so the local application does not receive the configured GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL.
raw_findings.root_cause: The env-file path is relative to the process working directory, not the script location.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compute the repository/script directory from `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` and set ENV_FILE to the intended repository .env using that absolute path.
raw_findings.title: Resolve the env file relative to the script rather than the caller
raw_findings.trigger: Running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root, which is the normal invocation for a script under scripts/.

raw_findings.body: GNU sed does not support the BSD `-i ''` form, so the replacement fails and the existing webhook URL remains unchanged despite the script subsequently announcing success.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Existing webhook configuration cannot be updated on Linux.
raw_findings.impact: GNU sed does not support the BSD `-i ''` form, so the replacement fails and the existing webhook URL remains unchanged despite the script subsequently announcing success.
raw_findings.root_cause: The script hard-codes BSD sed's separate empty backup suffix syntax.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a portable temporary-file replacement, or select the BSD/GNU in-place syntax based on the platform and check the command result.
raw_findings.title: Use a sed invocation that works on GNU/Linux
raw_findings.trigger: Running the script on GNU/Linux when GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is already present in the env file.

raw_findings.body: The script exits successfully even though it did not configure a usable webhook URL, preventing shells, wrappers, and CI-like callers from detecting the failed setup.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Setup failures are reported as successful command executions.
raw_findings.impact: The script exits successfully even though it did not configure a usable webhook URL, preventing shells, wrappers, and CI-like callers from detecting the failed setup.
raw_findings.root_cause: A cleanup helper used for both teardown and error handling unconditionally exits with status 0.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Allow cleanup to accept an exit status and invoke it with a nonzero status from setup-error paths; keep zero only for intentional interruption/successful teardown.
raw_findings.title: Return a failure status when tunnel setup fails
raw_findings.trigger: Tunnelmole hits its rate limit or no tunnel URL can be extracted, both of which call cleanup.

raw_findings.body: The localized cache-status label is paired with an English/US-formatted date and time, producing incorrect locale conventions for the user.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Internationalized UI displays dates in the wrong regional format.
raw_findings.impact: The localized cache-status label is paired with an English/US-formatted date and time, producing incorrect locale conventions for the user.
raw_findings.root_cause: The formatter is explicitly pinned to en-US instead of the locale already used for translations.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the active application locale to Intl.DateTimeFormat, or omit the hard-coded locale so the user's locale is used.
raw_findings.title: Format the cache timestamp using the active locale
raw_findings.trigger: A user whose Cal.com/browser locale is not en-US opens the calendar credential actions menu.

raw_findings.body: The ellipsis-only button has no textual accessible name, so assistive technology announces an unlabeled button and users cannot identify that it opens cache/disconnect actions.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The new actions menu is not reliably discoverable through assistive technology.
raw_findings.impact: The ellipsis-only button has no textual accessible name, so assistive technology announces an unlabeled button and users cannot identify that it opens cache/disconnect actions.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly introduced icon-only Button supplies neither visible text nor an accessibility label.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a localized aria-label describing the credential actions menu (and add the corresponding translation if needed).
raw_findings.title: Give the icon-only actions trigger an accessible name
raw_findings.trigger: A keyboard or screen-reader user reaches the credential actions control.

raw_findings.body: tRPC treats the generic Error as an internal server error rather than a client authorization/not-found response, causing clients and monitoring to see a 500-class failure for an expected rejected request.
raw_findings.evidence: throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied");
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authorization failures are exposed with the wrong API error classification.
raw_findings.impact: tRPC treats the generic Error as an internal server error rather than a client authorization/not-found response, causing clients and monitoring to see a 500-class failure for an expected rejected request.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new public mutation uses an untyped JavaScript Error for an expected access-control outcome.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Throw a TRPCError with the appropriate NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN code instead of a generic Error.
raw_findings.title: Return a typed authorization error for inaccessible credentials
raw_findings.trigger: An authenticated caller invokes deleteCache with a credential ID that is missing or belongs to another user.

validated_findings.impact: The migration documentation incorrectly says the operation cannot work on a populated table even though the added SQL supplies a default, creating unnecessary deployment concern and misleading future edits.
validated_findings.root_cause: The generated warning was retained after the migration SQL was changed to add a default.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Delete or update the generated warning so it accurately states that the column is added with a default.
validated_findings.title: Remove the contradictory migration warning
validated_findings.trigger: A maintainer reviews or troubleshoots this migration.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R4 states 'without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty' but line R9 shows `DEFAULT NOW()` is present. The warning comment contradicts the actual SQL, creating misleading documentation.

validated_findings.body: The script writes to the parent directory's .env instead of the repository .env, so the local application does not receive the configured GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A successful-looking run modifies an unrelated environment file.
validated_findings.impact: The script writes to the parent directory's .env instead of the repository .env, so the local application does not receive the configured GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL.
validated_findings.root_cause: The env-file path is relative to the process working directory, not the script location.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compute the repository/script directory from `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` and set ENV_FILE to the intended repository .env using that absolute path.
validated_findings.title: Resolve the env file relative to the script rather than the caller
validated_findings.trigger: Running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root, which is the normal invocation for a script under scripts/.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R5 shows `ENV_FILE="../.env"` which is relative to working directory. When run from repo root via `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, this resolves to parent of repo root, not the repo's .env file.

validated_findings.body: GNU sed does not support the BSD `-i ''` form, so the replacement fails and the existing webhook URL remains unchanged despite the script subsequently announcing success.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Existing webhook configuration cannot be updated on Linux.
validated_findings.impact: GNU sed does not support the BSD `-i ''` form, so the replacement fails and the existing webhook URL remains unchanged despite the script subsequently announcing success.
validated_findings.root_cause: The script hard-codes BSD sed's separate empty backup suffix syntax.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use a portable temporary-file replacement, or select the BSD/GNU in-place syntax based on the platform and check the command result.
validated_findings.title: Use a sed invocation that works on GNU/Linux
validated_findings.trigger: Running the script on GNU/Linux when GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is already present in the env file.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R68 shows `sed -i '' -E` which is BSD sed syntax. GNU sed requires `sed -i -E` (no space after -i for no backup). This will fail on Linux systems.

validated_findings.body: The script exits successfully even though it did not configure a usable webhook URL, preventing shells, wrappers, and CI-like callers from detecting the failed setup.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Setup failures are reported as successful command executions.
validated_findings.impact: The script exits successfully even though it did not configure a usable webhook URL, preventing shells, wrappers, and CI-like callers from detecting the failed setup.
validated_findings.root_cause: A cleanup helper used for both teardown and error handling unconditionally exits with status 0.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Allow cleanup to accept an exit status and invoke it with a nonzero status from setup-error paths; keep zero only for intentional interruption/successful teardown.
validated_findings.title: Return a failure status when tunnel setup fails
validated_findings.trigger: Tunnelmole hits its rate limit or no tunnel URL can be extracted, both of which call cleanup.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines R56-R58 show that when TUNNEL_URL extraction fails, `cleanup` is called which unconditionally `exit 0` per line R17. This masks setup failures from callers.

validated_findings.body: The localized cache-status label is paired with an English/US-formatted date and time, producing incorrect locale conventions for the user.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Internationalized UI displays dates in the wrong regional format.
validated_findings.impact: The localized cache-status label is paired with an English/US-formatted date and time, producing incorrect locale conventions for the user.
validated_findings.root_cause: The formatter is explicitly pinned to en-US instead of the locale already used for translations.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the active application locale to Intl.DateTimeFormat, or omit the hard-coded locale so the user's locale is used.
validated_findings.title: Format the cache timestamp using the active locale
validated_findings.trigger: A user whose Cal.com/browser locale is not en-US opens the calendar credential actions menu.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R89 shows `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` hardcoded while the app uses `useLocale()` for translations. Users with non-US locales see localized labels but US-formatted dates.

validated_findings.body: The ellipsis-only button has no textual accessible name, so assistive technology announces an unlabeled button and users cannot identify that it opens cache/disconnect actions.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The new actions menu is not reliably discoverable through assistive technology.
validated_findings.impact: The ellipsis-only button has no textual accessible name, so assistive technology announces an unlabeled button and users cannot identify that it opens cache/disconnect actions.
validated_findings.root_cause: The newly introduced icon-only Button supplies neither visible text nor an accessibility label.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a localized aria-label describing the credential actions menu (and add the corresponding translation if needed).
validated_findings.title: Give the icon-only actions trigger an accessible name
validated_findings.trigger: A keyboard or screen-reader user reaches the credential actions control.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R79 shows `<Button type="button" variant="icon" color="secondary" StartIcon="ellipsis" />` with no text content or aria-label. Icon-only buttons require accessible names for screen readers.

validated_findings.body: tRPC treats the generic Error as an internal server error rather than a client authorization/not-found response, causing clients and monitoring to see a 500-class failure for an expected rejected request.
validated_findings.evidence: throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied");
validated_findings.failure_mode: Authorization failures are exposed with the wrong API error classification.
validated_findings.impact: tRPC treats the generic Error as an internal server error rather than a client authorization/not-found response, causing clients and monitoring to see a 500-class failure for an expected rejected request.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new public mutation uses an untyped JavaScript Error for an expected access-control outcome.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Throw a TRPCError with the appropriate NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN code instead of a generic Error.
validated_findings.title: Return a typed authorization error for inaccessible credentials
validated_findings.trigger: An authenticated caller invokes deleteCache with a credential ID that is missing or belongs to another user.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R25 shows `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In tRPC, plain Error becomes INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500). Should use TRPCError with NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN code for proper HTTP status.
